## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The defaults-file deletion must be fixed before merge because it breaks `load_defaults()`. The port boundary and silent configuration failures should also be fixed; this review additionally found missing trailing-dot coverage and an inaccurate docstring.

## Critical
- app/defaults.json:1 [base] — correctness — Calling `load_defaults()` after this deletion raises `FileNotFoundError`. The unchanged reader at `app/startup.py:6` still opens this exact file. Restore the file or update the reader to obtain equivalent defaults. — Callers can no longer load the application's default configuration.

## Important
- app/parse.py:22 — correctness — `is_valid_port(65535)` returns `False`, rejecting the valid upper endpoint of the documented range. The comparison uses `< 65535`; change it to `<= 65535` and add an upper-bound test. — Users cannot select port 65535 through this validator.
- app/parse.py:30 — silent-failure — Loading malformed JSON returns `{}`, making a decoding failure indistinguishable from a successfully loaded empty configuration. `except Exception` also swallows file-access errors without logging or notifying the caller. Let read and decoding failures propagate so callers can identify and handle them. — Users receive no actionable indication that their configuration failed to load.
- app/parse.py:40 — tests — For `normalize_host("Example.COM.")`, the trailing-dot removal branch has no test coverage. The existing normalization test uses `"Example.COM"`, which skips this branch. Add a test asserting that the trailing-dot input produces `"example.com"`. — A regression that stops removing trailing dots would pass the current tests.

## Suggestions
- app/parse.py:35 — comments — For `normalize_host("")`, the docstring promises “returns None when h is empty,” while the implementation executes `return ""`. Update the docstring to describe the empty-string result. — Callers relying on the documentation could incorrectly check for `None`.

## Strengths
- The millisecond timeout test verifies the fractional result for `"1500ms"`.
- The configuration-loading test verifies decoded content from an actual temporary file.
